# 16. Lint generated files and give each one the full generated header

Date: 2026-10-18

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Every generated file carries one line: `Generated by "go generate
./..." from <source>. Do not edit by hand.` A Go file carries no
`Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.` marker, because golangci-lint skips
the findings of a file that has one, and rule 8 of
[ADR 0007, adopt testify assert and require in tests](0007-adopt-testify-assert-and-require-in-tests.md)
silences no finding. So a reader of a generated Go file, and the tools
that look for the marker (editors, `gopls`, code review), cannot tell
it is generated, and no generated file names the command that writes
it the way mockgen does:

```go
// Code generated by MockGen. DO NOT EDIT.
// Source: example_test.go
//
// Generated by this command:
//
//	mockgen -destination mock_test.go -package gomock_test -source example_test.go
//
```

What we measured (2026-10-18, golangci-lint v2.14.0, the version
`mise.toml` pins): `linters.exclusions.generated` takes `lax`,
`strict` (the default) or `disable`
(`pkg/config/linters_exclusions.go`). With `disable` the generated-file
filter returns every finding as it is
(`pkg/result/processors/exclusion_generated_file_filter.go`). One
linter skips such a file on its own: golangci-lint always passes
`ignore-generated-header: false` to revive
(`pkg/golinters/revive/revive.go`, with the comment that it should be
managed by `linters.exclusions.generated`), and revive v1.17.0 then
drops a file with a line that starts with `// Code generated ` and ends
with ` DO NOT EDIT.` before any rule runs (`lint/linter.go`). The
fixture test of the lint step showed it: gocritic and every testifylint
checker report in a file with the marker, and revive reports nothing
there.

Other linters decide on their own too. staticcheck v0.8.1, the one
golangci-lint bundles, drops the findings of these checks in a
generated file, and no setting turns that off (`report.FilterGenerated`
and `code.IsGenerated` in its source): S1000 to S1012, S1016 to S1021,
S1023 to S1025, S1028, S1030 to S1035, S1037 to S1040, SA4003, SA4018,
SA4019, SA4021, SA9003, SA9005, ST1001, ST1003, ST1006, ST1013, ST1015,
ST1016, ST1017, ST1019 to ST1023 and QF1011. SA4000, SA4006 and SA1019
skip a narrow case only (two zero literals, goyacc output, protoc-gen-go
output). golangci-lint's default leaves ST1003, ST1016 and ST1020 to
ST1022 off in any file (`pkg/golinters/staticcheck/staticcheck.go`).
Every other check reads a generated file. `unused`
counts every object of a generated file as used while its setting
`generated-is-used` is true, the default of golangci-lint
(`pkg/config/linters_settings.go`, and `unused/unused.go` of
staticcheck). go vet's stdversion pass drops its findings in a
generated file (`go/analysis/passes/stdversion/stdversion.go` of
golang.org/x/tools).

## Decision

1. **The linters read generated files.** `.golangci.yml` sets
   `linters.exclusions.generated: disable`, the one exclusion key it
   holds, and `generated-is-used: false` for `unused`. The test that
   runs the pinned linter over one violation of each checker, an unused
   function and a staticcheck check among them, runs it again over the
   same violations in files that carry the marker, so a proven checker
   that starts to skip a generated file fails the build. revive is the
   one proven checker that skips one, and the test holds it: revive
   reports nothing in those files. What revive would
   find there, the two rules of rule 14 of ADR 0001 it owns, is held by
   a test of the lint step instead: a Go file with the marker declares
   no exported identifier and calls neither `errors.New` nor
   `fmt.Errorf`. When golangci-lint lets revive read generated files,
   that test of revive's skip fails, and the guard goes. The
   staticcheck checks and the stdversion pass above stay skipped in a
   generated file, and that is accepted: only an output of `go generate`
   may carry the marker (the guard refuses it in any other Go file), the
   code of every generator is linted in full, and the generated check
   holds each output to what its generator writes. Rule 8 of ADR 0007
   changes with this record: the generated-code header is no longer
   refused, and the rule names what still skips a generated file.
2. **The full generated header.** Every file `go generate ./...`
   writes opens, after the lines that must come first (the SPDX lines
   of a Go file, the front matter of a page), with this header, in the
   comment syntax of the file:

   ```text
   Code generated by tools/ci generate. DO NOT EDIT.
   Source: <the files it is generated from> (<what in them>)

   Generated by this command:

   	go generate ./...
   ```

   In a Go file each line starts with `//` (`//` alone on an empty
   line), so the first line matches the convention of `go help
   generate`; `.github/CODEOWNERS` uses `#`; a Markdown page holds it in
   one HTML comment. The command is always `go generate ./...`, the one
   directive of the repository (12 12.3). Decision 7 of
   [ADR 0015, adopt spf13/cobra for the command line of romeu and julieta](0015-adopt-spf13-cobra-for-the-command-line-of-romeu-and-julieta.md)
   changes with this record: a `*_gen.go` file carries the header.

## Consequences

- REQ-1117 (12 12.3) defines the header for every generated file, and
  the list of 10 10.2 no longer refuses a generated-code header; it
  refuses any other value of `linters.exclusions.generated`.
- Editors, `gopls` and review tools see a generated Go file as
  generated, and every generated file names its source and the command
  that writes it.
- `tools/ci/internal/check` and `internal/cli` each write the header,
  since `internal/` cannot import `tools/ci/internal/`; a test of
  `tools/ci` holds the two to the same text.
- A future linter that skips generated code on its own is caught by
  the fixture test only if it is one of the checkers the fixtures
  prove; the default linters are not proven one by one today, and
  neither are the staticcheck checks beyond the one fixture.
- A simplification, a style check of staticcheck or a stdversion
  finding in a generated Go file goes unreported, so it is found in
  review of the generator or not at all. Today the one generated Go
  file holds a single string constant.
- A generated Go file that needs an exported identifier or an error
  string waits for revive to read generated files; the guard says so
  when it fails. The guard also fails a Go file with the marker that is
  no output of `go generate`, so a hand-written file cannot carry it.
- The guard copies revive v1.17.0's rule for a generated file. A bump
  of golangci-lint that brings another revive re-reads that rule
  (`isGenerated` in revive's `lint/linter.go`).
